route.title: The Word-Event Superscription
route.marker: The nominal word-event and addressee heading completes in 1:1 before the plural imperative 'Hear' opens direct public exhortation at 1:2.
route.rationale: Joel 1:1 is a complete prophetic superscription; the switch to plural commands in 1:2 changes both form and audience, so the heading remains a distinct child inside the hydrated opening parent.
route.rejected: Using Joel 1:1-12 as the only child would conceal the formal title seam, while surfacing 1:1 without the 1:1-12 parent would detach provenance from the crisis summons.
route.basis: A self-contained word-event formula supplies provenance and addressee, then the next verse begins a hear-and-tell act addressed to elders and inhabitants.
route.counter: The superscription has immediate rhetorical dependence on the hearing summons and should never be treated as context-complete by itself.
route.guard: Mandatory hydration through the opening crisis parent prevents the heading from becoming an authorship or chronology key.

route.title: Hear, Remember, and Tell the Devastation
route.marker: The elder-and-inhabitant summons advances through comparison and intergenerational telling to the completed fourfold loss catalogue at 1:4; 'Wake up' introduces a new audience in 1:5.
route.rationale: The commands to hear, test communal memory, and transmit the event culminate in the locust-loss refrain; the drunkard address at 1:5 begins a different lament sequence.
route.rejected: Merging 1:2-12 would blur the change from communal witnessing to successive vocatives, whereas dividing before 1:4 would strand the devastation recital that answers the opening questions.
route.basis: Questions about remembered precedent and instructions to tell later generations need the four-stage loss report as their content, producing a short complete summons-and-refrain form.
route.counter: The agricultural lament continues the same disaster and therefore requires the 1:1-12 parent even though its addressee changes.
route.guard: The parent preserves the relation between public memory, locust imagery, and the following human responses without identifying the disaster.

route.title: Serial Address-Lament over the Withered Land
route.marker: A chain of wake, weep, and lament addresses expands from drinkers through land and cultivators until the repeated withering language closes with joy itself at 1:12.
route.rationale: The shifting addressees and crop images form one escalating lament whose final claim that joy has withered completes the movement before priests receive new ritual imperatives.
route.rejected: Splitting at every vocative or crop would atomize the accumulation; merging 1:13-14 would absorb a priestly fast-and-assembly enactment into descriptive lament.
route.basis: Drunkards, land, farmers, and vine keepers are successive participants in one loss panorama, and recurring shame, mourning, and withering vocabulary binds their speeches.
route.counter: The passage continues the fourfold devastation of 1:4, making 1:2-12 a plausible larger reading movement despite the fresh imperative at 1:5.
route.guard: Keeping the opening parent available prevents locust, army, famine, and historical-event identities from being inferred from a child boundary.

route.title: Priestly Lament, Fast, and Assembly Summons
route.marker: Priestly sackcloth and overnight lament lead into commands to sanctify a fast, gather elders and inhabitants, and cry to Yahweh; 'Alas for the day' resets the form at 1:15.
route.rationale: The priestly imperatives reach their enacted goal in a consecrated communal gathering and cry, after which 1:15 begins a descriptive Day-of-Yahweh lament rather than another assembly command.
route.rejected: A single 1:13-20 child preserves cumulative response but suppresses the marked exclamation and form change at 1:15; ending at 1:13 would leave the fast summons unfinished.
route.basis: Sackcloth, altar service, fasting, gathering, and petition are coordinated ritual actions whose imperative chain closes before the day lament names and depicts the crisis.
route.counter: The commanded cry is immediately voiced and interpreted in 1:15-20, so the two children remain tightly dependent within one response parent.
route.guard: Parent hydration blocks the fast summons from being extracted as a timeless mandate or separated from the devastation that occasions it.

route.title: Day Lament and Creation's Cry
route.marker: The day exclamation opens a lament over food, worship, seed, stores, herds, fire, and water, ending when the prophet and animals direct their need to Yahweh at 1:20.
route.rationale: The Day-of-Yahweh exclamation governs an expanding deprivation catalogue that resolves in direct prayer and the animals' panting, completing the crisis response before a new Zion trumpet sounds.
route.rejected: Isolating 1:19-20 would detach the prayer from the losses it voices; recombining 1:13-20 would hide the shift from commanded assembly to narrated lament.
route.basis: Day language, sanctuary deprivation, ruined seed, distressed herds, consuming fire, and failed water converge in a single lament whose final addressee supplies closure.
route.counter: The preceding fast summons supplies the liturgical setting for the cry and remains necessary context for the first-person turn.
route.guard: The response parent prevents day language or creation distress from being mapped onto a fixed chronology or disaster mechanism.

route.title: Zion Alarm and the Advancing Host
route.marker: The Zion trumpet opens an alarm describing the approaching day, ordered host, breached city, cosmic shaking, and Yahweh's climactic voice before 2:12 begins direct return speech.
route.rationale: Alarm, host description, similes, urban advance, cosmic disturbance, and the final endurance question form one intensifying oracle bounded by the explicit return appeal at 2:12.
route.rejected: Dividing at 2:10 would sever cosmic signs from the voice and endurance climax; extending through 2:17 would merge the threat depiction with its appeal-and-intercession answer.
route.basis: Repeated trumpet, day, host, movement, and cosmic motifs progress toward the closing endurance question rather than forming detachable image lists.
route.counter: The ensuing return summons is the intended rhetorical response, so the 2:1-17 parent must accompany retrieval of the alarm.
route.guard: Hydration with the return movement prevents the host, locust, northern force, or day imagery from being assigned an identity or timetable.

route.title: Return, Assemble, and Intercede
route.marker: The divine 'Yet even now' return appeal proceeds through character confession and possible blessing into a renewed trumpet, comprehensive assembly, and the priests' quoted plea at 2:17.
route.rationale: Return, communal enactment, and priestly intercession make one appeal-to-response sequence; the renewed trumpet at 2:15 is a real internal reset but does not outweigh completion in the plea.
route.rejected: Dividing 2:12-14 from 2:15-17 honors the imperative reset, yet it separates the called-for return from its corporate and priestly enactment.
route.basis: Direct divine appeal supplies motive and uncertainty, while assembly instructions and quoted prayer perform that appeal publicly before the response begins at 2:18.
route.counter: The second trumpet and change from divine speech to communal instructions support two locally coherent submovements and remain indexed internally.
route.guard: The alarm parent keeps repentance, ritual, divine character, and possible blessing together without converting their sequence into a doctrinal mechanism.

route.title: Response, Removal, and Restored Provision
route.marker: The jealousy-and-pity response introduces provision and removal, then reassurances to land, animals, and Zion carry the reversal through restitution, recognition, and the repeated no-shame close.
route.rationale: The narrated response, removal promise, three reassurance addresses, agricultural repair, restitution, and recognition refrain belong to one sustained reversal of the preceding devastation.
route.rejected: Splitting after 2:20 honors the address change at 2:21 but detaches restoration from its response; merging through 2:32 crosses the 'afterward' formula.
route.basis: Response verbs open the oracle, repeated 'great things' language bridges 2:20-21, and the double no-shame formula closes removal, provision, and restored knowledge.
route.counter: New vocatives to land, animals, and Zion create a genuine poetic turn after the removal oracle and may aid internal navigation.
route.guard: The unit must not settle the northern one's referent, the teacher/rain rendering, permanence, or a chronology of restoration.

route.title: Outpouring, Portents, and Escape
route.marker: The temporal formula 'It will happen afterward' opens the proclamation; inclusive recipients, portents, invocation, escape, and called remnant close at 2:32 before a nations-judgment frame.
route.rationale: Outpouring, social breadth, prophetic speech, signs, day language, invocation, and remnant escape constitute one proclamation whose final deliverance clause completes the movement.
route.rejected: Splitting at 2:31 detaches escape from the portents; joining 3:1-3 as the only unit suppresses the nations frame and lets versification decide the seam.
route.basis: The 'afterward' opening and closing Zion-Jerusalem escape declaration bracket a sequence coherent across the WEB-to-Hebrew chapter-number offset.
route.counter: Temporal linkage continues into 3:1, and later reuse can make an isolated child appear to decide fulfillment or Spirit theology.
route.guard: Acts, Romans, and other reuse are hydration evidence only; the 2:28-3:21 parent protects against back-projecting later interpretation.

route.title: Nations Judgment Announced
route.marker: The 'For, behold, in those days' frame announces restoration, gathering, judicial pleading, scattering, land division, lots, and trafficking before 3:4 turns to named defendants.
route.rationale: Verses 1-3 establish the nations courtroom and its general indictment; direct questions to named neighbors at 3:4 justify provisional separation while the whole lawsuit remains the parent.
route.rejected: Treating 3:1-8 as one child preserves the complete judicial scene, whereas a hard split at 3:4 risks detaching the repayment speech from its introducing charges.
route.basis: A temporal-and-judicial frame names gathering, controversy, and initial offenses, then a direct-address formula changes the discourse relation without ending the lawsuit.
route.counter: The general charges are concretized by named accusations and reciprocal verdict in 3:4-8, making autonomous retrieval materially contestable.
route.guard: The 2:28-3:21 and 3:1-8 parents prevent versification, modern nation mapping, chronology, or fulfillment claims from following the provisional seam.

route.title: Named Neighbors Addressed and Repaid
route.marker: The formula 'Yes, and what are you to me?' names Tyre, Sidon, and Philistia, shifts to second-person accusation, and carries reciprocal repayment through 3:8.
route.rationale: Named defendants, direct questions, specific offenses, and a reciprocal verdict give 3:4-8 a provisional oracle shape, but dependence on the general indictment requires a paired hold.
route.rejected: Merging 3:1-8 keeps accusation and verdict together yet hides a strong addressee seam; retrieving 3:4-8 alone obscures why the named parties enter the lawsuit.
route.basis: A distinct vocative field and second-person exchange open at 3:4, while announced repayment and the closing speech formula provide an identifiable close.
route.counter: The speech develops rather than replaces the preceding nations case, so evidence does not yet prove an autonomous top-level child.
route.guard: Mandatory 3:1-8 hydration guards against extracting violence, enslavement language, or geographic names into modern ethical and political claims.

route.title: War Muster, Judicial Harvest, and Zion Refuge
route.marker: The proclamation begins a muster drawing nations to judicial sitting, harvest and winepress imagery, cosmic disturbance, divine roar, refuge, and the recognition close at 3:17.
route.rationale: The war summons names the participants whom the judge gathers, and their arrival advances directly into harvest judgment, cosmic climax, refuge, and Zion recognition as one scene.
route.rejected: Dividing 3:9-11 from 3:12-17 honors the speaker transition but separates the muster from its judicial purpose; ending at 3:16 strands the recognition close.
route.basis: Imperatives assemble the nations, judicial speech explains their destination, and harvest, multitudes, darkness, roar, refuge, and holiness complete the confrontation.
route.counter: The appeal at 3:11 and first-person judicial declaration at 3:12 create a real speaker boundary suitable for internal navigation.
route.guard: The unit cannot authorize holy-war ethics, identify modern nations, harmonize other judgment scenes, or impose an eschatological sequence.

route.title: Abundance, Contrast, and Yahweh Dwelling in Zion
route.marker: The formula 'It will happen in that day' opens abundance; fountain, contrasting desolation, enduring Judah and Jerusalem, the difficult blood clause, and Yahweh's dwelling close the book.
route.rationale: The new day formula introduces a restoration coda whose water, land contrast, enduring community, unresolved blood wording, and final Zion-dwelling line form the closing tableau.
route.rejected: Merging 3:9-21 suppresses the coda formula after the recognition climax; splitting 3:19-21 detaches contrast and final dwelling from abundance.
route.basis: Agricultural abundance and flowing water establish reversal, Egypt and Edom supply contrast, and paired Jerusalem-and-dwelling statements bring formal closure.
route.counter: Zion, refuge, holiness, and dwelling continue 3:16-17, while the blood clause remains textually and translationally difficult.
route.guard: Retrieval must hydrate the prior Zion climax and must not choose a reading for 3:21 or turn dwelling imagery into a political or fulfillment ruling.
